question: Does JUXTAPOSE/SPIDER/KEYMASTER order finding retain a genuine total-compute advantage once compared against strong classical sqrt-scale order-finding baselines, and does a dual-core GEMINI fusion add anything beyond the best constituent core?

scale_ladder.fresh_case_generation: deterministic from frozen SHA256 seeds; no v1 holdout N values may be reused
scale_ladder.base_selection: first coprime a from deterministic sequence [2,3,5,7,11,13,17,19]

competitors.LINEAR_REFERENCE: sequential multiplication until a^r == 1; diagnostic only, not the v2 strong baseline
competitors.BSGS_ORDER: deterministic baby-step/giant-step-like order finder with O(sqrt(N)) table/walk scale and incremental group multiplication; exact-reduce any positive collision multiple to minimal order
competitors.RHO_COLLISION: deterministic-seeded generic collision walk; exact reduction required before a found order is accepted
competitors.JANUS_ORBIT: v1-style diversified exponent waves; SPIDER residue collisions; KEYMASTER gcd of collision gaps; EXACT_JANUS minimal-order certification
competitors.GEMINI_RELATION_V0: independent congruence-of-squares scout using Fermat-style x^2-y^2=N search; exact gcd/factor receipt only; explicitly not claimed to be Quadratic Sieve or NFS
competitors.GEMINI_FUSION_V0: ORBIT and RELATION run as independent cores; exact factor/order receipts may terminate useful postprocessing; total compute is the SUM of both cores up to termination, while latency is tracked separately

resource_accounting.total_compute_rule: never count parallel cores as free; GEMINI total compute sums constituent work
resource_accounting.memory_rule: BSGS table size and all core memory are explicit
resource_accounting.factor_generation_cost: excluded from solver runtime but factors are never passed into any solver

mad_lab.target: find fresh semiprime families where JANUS_ORBIT loses to BSGS_ORDER and where GEMINI_FUSION loses to the best single core after honest total-compute accounting

frozen_gates.criterion: all order-finding solvers that return FOUND must match independently certified order on 36/36 cases; JANUS_ORBIT must be exact on 36/36
report median ratio; PASS only if JANUS_ORBIT median primary group/modular-multiplication work <= BSGS_ORDER median work
PASS only if JANUS_ORBIT total-compute wins on >= 50% cases
fit log2(work) vs bit_length separately; PASS only if JANUS_ORBIT fitted slope is strictly lower than BSGS_ORDER by >= 0.05 on this finite ladder; descriptive, not asymptotic proof
PASS only if GEMINI_FUSION total compute beats min(ORBIT, RELATION) on >= 25% cases; because compute is summed, this is intentionally difficult
solver APIs receive only N,a and frozen public algorithm parameters
no quantum-speedup, polynomial-factoring, or P=NP claim from finite scaling data

allowed: Determine whether v1 JANUS collision behavior exceeds a strong classical sqrt-scale baseline on this ladder.
Determine whether GEMINI v0 fusion has measurable added value under honest total-compute accounting.
Use failures to redesign MAD-LAB and successor cores.
forbidden: Claim polynomial-time factoring from finite rung fits.
Claim equivalence to Shor quantum period finding.
Treat a lower fitted exponent on six rungs as a theorem.
